script.title: A Better Way to Care — Welbuk

script.style: Full-colour, approachable Indian slice-of-life manga. Clean confident line art with varied line weight, soft flat cel shading, warm natural daylight, restrained blue and teal accents, simple readable backgrounds. Expressive but natural faces, precise hands. No photorealism, no glossy gradients, no surface microtexture. Absolutely no text, letters, logos, numbers, speech bubbles or captions inside the artwork; device screens show only abstract blank blocks and simple icons.
script.continuity: Keep Dr. Ananya, Meera and Ravi identical to their canonical reference sheets in face traits, hair, build, skin tone and clothing for the whole comic. Device screens never show readable text or real personal data. Pages 6 panels 2-3 are a future vision: soft pale-blue vignette border and lighter, airy palette so they never read as current features.

pages.scan: Read the request JSON first. Then I opened the one image it lists, works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png, with Read and looked at it before reading anything else. The image was readable. It is a 4-panel storyboard: a wide panel across the top, two panels side by side in the middle (left and right), and a wide panel across the bottom. People are shown as grey placeholder boxes with dot labels 'ananya' and 'ravi'. Page number '4' is printed at the bottom. I did not read the source text, script, workflow.json, reading-flow files, earlier responses or the docs. The runtime did not give me a task identity, so task is null.
pages.observation: My natural reading order (left-to-right, top-to-bottom): (1) Top panel: 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' The tail points to the ananya box on the left. Ravi's box is upper right. The speaker is clearly Ananya. (2) Middle-left panel: 'I've been feeling tired lately.' The tail goes down-right to the left edge of the ravi box, so Ravi is the speaker. In this panel Ananya is only a dot label at the far left with no face/figure box, while Ravi has a box. (3) Middle-right panel: a square narration caption, 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' The ananya box is in the centre. Ravi is only a dot label right at the right border with no box. (4) Bottom panel: 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' The tail points to the ananya box on the left, so Ananya is the speaker. Ravi's box is on the right. I followed the order without trouble: there is one balloon or caption per panel, and none of them compete. Confusing or unresolved points: (a) The middle-right caption reads as an abstract, thematic statement. It breaks into the doctor-patient exchange right after Ravi says he is tired. Nobody reacts to his complaint, so the jump from 'tired lately' to a slogan-like narration and then to 'We'll go through your concerns' feels like a missing beat (a question, an acknowledgement, or a visible reaction from Ananya). On the image alone it is unclear whose voice the caption is (narrator? Ananya's thoughts?) and why 'technology' comes in. Nothing on this page shows any technology. (b) In panels 1 and 4 the tails sit on top of the 'ananya' labels, so the labels are partly hidden ('anany', 'ana..'). The speaker is still readable from tail direction, but the label placement should be checked. (c) Ravi's position is not consistent. He has a figure box in panels 1, 2 and 4, but in panel 3 he is a bare label against the right border, possibly cut off or offscreen, and his face area is not defined. Ananya likewise has no box in panel 2. If either person is meant to be visible, the face regions are missing. (d) The top panel is large but has one short greeting and a big empty lower half. Panel size versus importance should be reconsidered. Ravi's only line, the complaint that drives the scene, sits in a smaller panel. (e) Ananya is on the left and Ravi on the right in panels 1, 3 and 4, and in panel 2 his box is right of her label, so their screen sides stay the same across the page. Request changes: resolve the missing reaction/response beat around the caption, clarify the caption's voice and relevance, and define the visible faces/positions in panels 2 and 3.
